issue_context.title: Plugwise Smile Anna intermittent device not available
issue_context.body:
### The problem

My Plugwise Anna thermostat switches from available to not available every few minutes. If the device is available, it will switch to unavailable in about 1 minute and comes back a few minutes later.

The device can be accessed normally throug the web url directly and doesn't seem to have any connection issues there.
Disabled ipv6 to see if that resolved the issue, but same results. Ipv6 issues where mentioned in other ticket.

HA and Smile are on the same VLAN. HA has full access to the outside, other devices, like Smile, can only resolve DNS and get SNTP time.

There are no errors in the logs.

Let me know if more information is needed to solve this issue.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2022.11.1

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Plugwise

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/plugwise/

Is it only the Anna that switches from available to unavailable?
What about the OpenTherm device? Or the Smile Anna device?

Never mind, you have an OnOff-type device.

Can you roll back to 2022.10.5 and monitor something for me?
In the recent update we have included availability per device, for the Anna the maximum allowed time-interval between updates has been set to 90 seconds. It might be that this number is too small.
Will have a look tonight after work with 2022.10.5.

What to monitor: the difference between the `modified_date` updates for the Anna.
Please open `http://<smile_ip>/core/appliances` in a browser, you should see xml-data.
Look for this part:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11290930/200320806-2ac83d16-9fa9-4998-9cfb-3b1ed3fbe426.png)
Please focus on the `modified_date` line, on the timestamp.
When you see the timestamp change on your system, how much time is in between the changes?
On my system, the interval was never larger than 60 seconds. I expect that on your system this interval is larger.

Hi, I made a script to monitor the `modified_date` of Anna.
First is was polling every 10 seconds and the date changed arround every 5 minutes, but when I changed the polling time to 400 seconds, the modified_date was giving much higher deltas. The max difference I saw was even 2505 seconds, so ~42 minutes.

Wondering if this modified_date can even be used for detecting if Anna is offline.
There where a few 'connection denied' situations, but that is not from Anna specifically, that's the Smile.

Added monitor log.
[anna-modified.csv](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/files/9959353/anna-modified.csv)

@dotnetniet Thanks for the logging!
Indeed, it looks like the 90 seconds interval is very much too small!

Now, I have two options, remove the availability-option for the Anna, or set the interval to e.g. 60 minutes.
As far as I know, there is no other way to detect that the Anna has been disconnected. There is no notification in the Plugwise Anna has been disconnected. Which is there when the OpenTherm device has been connected.

Availability for Anna in an OnOff system is probably not needed. This monitor log is only from a small timespan, so it does not give the full picture. Think in the Summer it can take even longer for the modified_date to change.

I also found another problem with `central_heating_state` and `intended_central_heating_state` for my system. Should I make a new issue for that?

Ok, then I'll remove the device availability for the Anna. I'll keep you posted on the progress of this.

On the other topic, yes, please create a new issue.
Thanks, much appreciated. Let's make this even better then it already is 👍

Good morning @bouwew,

Should this line not ignore the `and not data.get("heating_state")` for the Anna?
https://github.com/plugwise/python-plugwise/blob/0da50f9640ee10b2d450dbe9519b3ca99df3df5f/plugwise/helper.py#L999
It does not harm to have it there. Also, when Plugwise decides to change, switch to using intended_central_heating_state, it'll still work.

Still a boolean compare with a value that is unpredictable or is not related to an OnOff system seems to be incorrect. 

Edit: just noticed that this remark should be part of issue #81839 my bad.
@dotnetniet the above-mentioned line will be removed in the plugwise-library v0.25.13, I'll try to add this update to HA Core ASAP.

@bouwew, device is not offline anymore, thanks.

I also needed to fix the network access of the Smiley to the outside, because it tries to get the local weather information and if some firewall rule does not allow that, the device will freeze for a minute. No new connections can be made at that time and the device is then really offline.
It's a limitation of these devices that can only be fixed by a firmware update, but that will probably not happen...

Have a good day and thanks again for these fixes for our OnOff systems 🙂

Yes, when an update fails, the api is empty/None.
It has been removed in a follow up PR that implemented the ConfigEntryErrors.
The name was remove/lost, was this intentional?
Yes. No/empty api when the connection fails.
This error was related to the Anna-connected-to-Adam case. It is now handled in the config_flow, you added some code covering this case some time ago. So removed from the library in this update.

> It is now handled in the config_flow, you added some code covering this case some time ago. So removed from the library in this update.

That is not solving the manual flow. The code added to the config flow handle the auto-discovery. The code now removed handled the manual path.

Oh, sorry, then I've misunderstood that change.
I'll put it back in plugwise v0.25.12
